thesis: Ar-Ra'd's opening presents the Book and the created world as one single field of ayat, so that reading creation rightly produces certainty about the meeting with Allah.
notes: No fix needed. Thesis is carried by the tafsir itself: al-Tabari on 13:2 glosses 'yufassilu al-ayat ... la'allakum bi-liqa'i rabbikum tuqinun' as Allah clarifying His book's signs so that 'you may be certain of the meeting with Him and the return to Him' (quoting Qatadah: 'Allah sent down His book and sent His messengers so that we believe His promise and are certain of His meeting'). Ibn Kathir on 13:3-4 makes the same move from the higher world to the lower one as evidence of the one Creator. Verified mechanically against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json: the faculty sequence the file builds on is real - 13:2:26 تُوقِنُ root يقن, 13:3:24 يَتَفَكَّرُ root فكر, 13:4:27 يَعْقِلُ root عقل, exactly in that ayah order. The sinwan attribution 'The classical explanation is that some share one root-stock while others stand on separate roots' matches Ibn Kathir verbatim in substance ('Sinwan means growing into two or three from a single stem ... Ghayru Sinwan means having one stem for every tree'); root صنو confirmed at 13:4:10 and 13:4:12. 'mutajawirat - adjoining, side by side' matches Ibn Kathir ('next to each other'); root جور confirmed at 13:4:4. yudabbiru/yufassilu glosses match al-Tabari ('yaqdi ... umura al-dunya wa al-akhirah kullaha wahdahu' / 'yufassilu lakum rabbukum ayati kitabihi fa-yubayyinuha lakum'). No countable or hapax claims are made anywhere in the file. No tafsir is quoted directly, so there are no truncation artifacts. The same-water/different-fruit-as-hearts reading in Theme 1 is correctly presented as contemplation, not attribution ('One way to sit with the image ...', 'Ar-Ra'd does not reduce all of that mystery to one simple answer, but it does give us a physical parable for it'). One observation only, not a defect: the file passes over the well-known ikhtilaf on 13:2 (Ibn Abbas/Mujahid: 'with pillars you cannot see' vs Iyas b. Mu'awiyah/Qatadah and al-Tabari's own preference: no pillars at all) and on 'tilka ayatu al-kitab' (Qatadah/Mujahid read al-kitab as the Torah and Injil, distinct from what was sent to the Prophet). It makes no assertion on either, so nothing is false; a future enrichment pass could add the pillars ikhtilaf as a one-line note.

thesis: Faithful witness is measured not by controlling people's reactions but by staying bound to revelation while refusing forms of speech that predictably provoke a greater violation.

flags.quote: This is not abandonment of da'wah. It is refusal of certain futile entanglements. Sometimes fidelity requires disengaging from argument patterns that only recycle resistance.
flags.issue: Rubric check 4 (ahkam adab on a contested/interfaith passage). The file reads 'wa a'rid 'ani al-mushrikin' (6:106) as a permanent, universally applicable da'wah posture and never mentions that this exact phrase is the subject of a well-documented classical ikhtilaf. al-Tabari, immediately after giving the same plain-sense gloss the file uses ('da' 'anka jidalahum wa khusumatahum'), records: 'thumma nasakha dhalika jalla thana'uhu bi-qawlihi fi Bara'ah: fa-qtulu al-mushrikina haythu wajadtumuhum' [9:5], with the isnad to Ibn Abbas via Ali b. Abi Talha stating that everything by which Allah commanded the believers to pardon the mushrikin was abrogated by 9:5. al-Jalalayn on 6:107 likewise notes 'wa hadha qabla al-amri bi-l-qital.' Ibn Kathir keeps 6:106 operative but reads it as temporary forbearance ('be forbearing and endure their harm UNTIL Allah brings relief to you, supports you and makes you triumphant over them') - which is not the timeless disengagement principle the file states. The file picks one side of a live abrogation dispute silently, on an interfaith verse, with no ikhtilaf acknowledgment and no tadabbur/fatwa distinction anywhere in the piece.

flags.quote: People are not neutral about what they inherited and normalized. They are emotionally invested in it. What they practice becomes beautified in their sight.
flags.issue: Rubric check 1/3 drift on 'kadhalika zayyanna li-kulli ummatin 'amalahum'. The file quotes the divine subject correctly one line earlier ('Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deed') and then glosses it as a purely human psychological mechanism, dropping the agency all four editions insist on. Ibn Kathir: 'as We made fair seeming to the idolators loving their idols and defending them, likewise We made fair seeming to every previous nation the misguidance they indulged in.' al-Tabari is more explicit still: 'kadhalika zayyanna li-kulli jama'atin ... 'amalahum alladhi hum 'alayhi mujtami'un' - and ties it to divine forsaking, 'bi-khidhlanina iyyahum 'an ta'ati al-Rahman'. al-Muyassar frames it as recompense: 'wa kama hassanna li-ha'ula'i 'amalahum al-sayyi' 'uqubatan lahum 'ala su'i ikhtiyarihim'. The file's gloss is not false as psychology but it silently replaces the tafsir's theological claim.

notes: The interfaith-adab concern raised in the assignment does NOT hold: the file's handling of 6:108 is grounded in the tafsir's own reasoning, not a modern tolerance framing. It states outright 'The issue is not that their objects of worship deserve reverence. They do not. The issue is consequence: Fa-yasubbu Allaha 'adwan bi-ghayri 'ilm.' That is exactly the classical sadd al-dhara'i logic - Ibn Kathir: 'Insulting their deities will lead to a bigger evil than its benefit, for the idolators might retaliate by insulting the God of the believers'; al-Muyassar says the word 'saddan li-l-dhari'ah' explicitly; al-Tabari carries the sabab (Quraysh telling the Prophet 'you will stop insulting our gods, or we will insult your Lord') via Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and al-Suddi. No fix needed there. The single fix required is on 6:106: add one sentence acknowledging that classical scholars disagreed over whether 'wa a'rid 'ani al-mushrikin' remained operative or was abrogated by 9:5 (al-Tabari records Ibn Abbas for abrogation; Ibn Kathir keeps it as forbearance until relief comes), and mark that this is tadabbur on the passage's ethic, not a fatwa on the ruling. Secondary fix: restore the divine subject in the zayyanna gloss. Everything else verifies. Mechanical check against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json confirms the only linguistic claim in the file - 6:105:2 نُصَرِّفُ root صرف, pos V - so 'the verb nusarrifu from the root s-r-f' is correct. The darasta gloss ('you have merely studied this elsewhere') matches Ibn Abbas via al-Tabari ('qara'ta wa ta'allamta', 'taqulu dhalika Quraysh') and al-Muyassar ('ta'allamta min ahli al-kitab'), and al-Tabari's qira'at discussion (darasta / darasta with alif / durisat / darasat) is not needed for the file's point. The hafiz/wakil distinction is exact: al-Tabari glosses hafiz as 'lam nab'athka hafizan 'alayhim ma hum 'amiluh, tuhsi dhalika 'alayhim' and wakil as 'lasta 'alayhim bi-qayyimin taqumu bi-arzaqihim wa aqwatihim'; the file's 'guardship, preserving, watching over outcomes' / 'management, disposal of affairs, delegated control' matches. The law-sha'a gloss avoids jabr and matches al-Muyassar. No countable, hapax or 'only place' claims appear. No tafsir is quoted directly, so no truncation artifacts.

thesis: The same Lord who takes upon Himself the clarification of the straight path is the One who sends the rain, brings out the provision, and orders the heavens, so hidayah and the ordered world are one coherent mercy rather than two separate domains.
notes: No fix needed. The thesis is not merely compatible with the tafsir - it is Ibn Kathir's own structural reading of the passage: 'When Allah mentioned the animals which may be used for the purpose of physical journeys, He also referred to the moral, religious routes that people may follow. Often in the Qur'an there is a shift from physical or tangible things to beneficial spiritual and religious matters.' The file's introduction ('After speaking about animals that carry you across land, the surah does something beautiful. It turns from roads on earth to the road of truth') reproduces that pivot faithfully. The one explicit attribution in the file - 'The tafsir tradition explains this as Allah's making clear, showing, and setting forth the path of truth for His servants' - verifies across all four editions: al-Tabari ('wa 'ala Allahi ayyuha al-nasu bayanu tariqi al-haqqi lakum') with isnads to Ibn Abbas ('al-bayan, an yubayyina al-huda wa al-dalalah'), Mujahid ('tariqu al-haqqi 'ala Allah'), Qatadah ('bayanu halalihi wa haramihi'), al-Dahhak ('inaratuha'); Ibn Kathir cites the same chain of names; al-Muyassar 'wa 'ala Allahi bayanu al-tariqi al-mustaqim'; al-Jalalayn 'ay bayanu al-tariqi al-mustaqim'. The lexical gloss on qasd ('directedness, straight intention, a path that aims truly and does not wander') matches al-Tabari's 'al-qasdu mina al-tariqi al-mustaqimu alladhi la i'wijaja fih'. Mechanically verified against scripts/.corpus-cache/quranic-corpus.json: the two-faculty seal the file builds on is real - 16:11:16 يَتَفَكَّرُ root فكر and 16:12:15 يَعْقِلُ root عقل, in that order; and the 'repetition of minhu' in 16:10 is confirmed (the corpus splits it as مِّنْ + هُ, so a naive whole-word search returns zero - after segment-joining, exactly two occurrences: 'lakum minhu sharabun wa minhu shajarun'). tusimun = 'you pasture' is the unanimous gloss (Ikrimah, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd all: tar'awn). No countable, hapax, 'only place' or 'never' claims appear anywhere. No tafsir is quoted directly, so no truncation artifacts. Adab note in the file's favour, not against it: al-Tabari and al-Muyassar both identify 'wa minha ja'ir' concretely with Judaism, Christianity and the other milal, and Ibn Kathir adds Zoroastrianism; the file deliberately keeps it general ('Some roads are bent. Some routes do not deliver where they promise') and names no community, which is the safer choice for a mixed-audience page. It also makes no assertion about the qadar clause 'wa law sha'a la-hadakum ajma'in' beyond reproducing it in the translation, so no contested theological claim is left unguarded.
